response: Proof: Since BN is an altitude, BN ⊥ AC, so ∠BNC = 90°. Since CM is an altitude, CM ⊥ AB, so ∠CMB = 90°. In triangle BMS, ∠BMS = 90° (since M lies on AB and SM lies along CM, which is perpendicular to AB) and ∠MSB = 40° (given), so by the angle sum of a triangle, ∠MBS = 180° − 90° − 40° = 50°. Since ∠SBC = 20° (given) and ∠MBC = ∠MBS + ∠SBC (because S lies inside the triangle, so ray BS lies between rays BM and BC), we get ∠ABC = ∠MBC = 50° + 20° = 70°. Now consider triangle BMC: ∠BMC = 90° (CM ⊥ AB), so ∠MCB = 180° − 90° − 70° = 20°. Since CS lies along CM, ∠SCB = ∠MCB = 20°. Thus ∠SCB = ∠SBC = 20°. Triangle SBC therefore has two equal angles at B and C, so by the converse of the isosceles triangle theorem, SB = SC. Next, we show ∠ACB = 70°: in triangle BNC, ∠BNC = 90° and ∠NBC = ∠SBC + ∠SBN; since ∠SBN is the angle in triangle SBN, we use the fact that ∠BSC = 180° − 20° − 20° = 140°, and ∠NSC is its supplement? Instead, note that ∠BSC and ∠MSB are supplementary because M, S, C are collinear: ∠BSC = 180° − ∠MSB = 180° − 40° = 140°, consistent with the above. Now in triangle BNC, ∠NBC = 90° − ∠ACB. Since ∠SCB = 20° and S lies on CM, the line CM is the altitude from C, so ∠ACM = 90° − ∠A, and in triangle AMC (right angle at M), ∠MCA = 90° − ∠A. Also, from triangle ABC, ∠A + ∠ABC + ∠ACB = 180°, with ∠ABC = 70°, so ∠A + ∠ACB = 110°. Since ∠MCB = 20° and ∠MCA = ∠ACB − ∠MCB = ∠ACB − 20°, and ∠MCA = 90° − ∠A, we have ∠ACB − 20° = 90° − ∠A, so ∠ACB + ∠A = 110°, which is consistent but gives no new information. Instead, use BN: BN is an altitude, so in right triangle BNC, ∠NBC = 90° − ∠ACB. Since ∠NBC = ∠SBC = 20° (BN passes through S, so ray BS = ray BN), we get 90° − ∠ACB = 20°, hence ∠ACB = 70°. Since ∠ABC = 70° and ∠ACB = 70°, triangle ABC has two equal angles at B and C, so by the converse of the isosceles triangle theorem, AB = AC. Therefore ΔABC is isosceles. ∎

• the sum of angles in any triangle is 180°.
• if two angles of a triangle are equal, the triangle is isosceles.
and possibly also uses:
• vertically opposite angles are equal.
• supplementary angles add to 180°.
The concept of congruence is not used.

  - Other responses with minor errors.

  - Other incorrect responses.
- Nonresponse (0 points):
